title: Find a cool space near you
summary: During heat warnings, the city lists air-conditioned public places you can go, including libraries, community centres and some civic buildings.
details: Use the city's Cool Spaces map to find the nearest one
Check hours before you go, since not all spaces are open evenings or weekends
If you need to check on someone, call 311 for the Heat Relief Network

sources.title: City of Toronto: Cool Spaces Near You
City of Toronto: Heat Relief

title: Check the AQHI before outdoor exercise
summary: Ontario publishes an hourly Air Quality Health Index for Toronto with advice for at-risk groups and for everyone else.
details: Look up the current AQHI for Toronto stations
At 7 or above, reduce or reschedule strenuous outdoor activity
People with heart or lung conditions should follow the at-risk advice at lower values

sources.title: Air Quality Ontario: AQHI
City of Toronto: Air Quality

title: Shift heavy electricity use to off-peak hours
summary: Ontario's time-of-use and ultra-low overnight rates charge less at night and on weekends. Running laundry, dishwashers and EV charging then costs less, and overnight demand is met with less gas generation.
details: Check which rate plan your bill uses: time-of-use, tiered, or ultra-low overnight
Ultra-low overnight is designed for EV owners and anyone who can run appliances after 11 p.m.
Set delay timers on the dishwasher and washer so the shift happens on its own

sources.title: Ontario Energy Board: Electricity rates

title: Free energy-saving upgrades for income-qualified households
summary: Save on Energy's Energy Affordability Program installs free upgrades, from LED bulbs to insulation and in some cases a heat pump, for households under the income limits. Renters qualify if the utility account is in their name.
details: Check the income limits on the program page (they scale by household size)
Anyone on Ontario Works, ODSP, OESP or LEAP in the past 12 months qualifies automatically
Apply online or call 1-844-770-3148

sources.title: Save on Energy: Energy Affordability Program

title: Home Renovation Savings rebates
summary: Ontario's Home Renovation Savings Program pays rebates on insulation, heat pumps, windows, smart thermostats and rooftop solar, whichever fuel heats your home.
details: Smart thermostat rebate is $100 with no assessment needed
Bigger upgrades like a cold-climate heat pump (up to $7,500) or insulation (up to $7,700) can go through a home energy assessment first
Apply on the Home Renovation Savings website

sources.title: Save on Energy: Home Renovation Savings Program
Home Renovation Savings

title: Home Energy Loan Program (HELP)
summary: The City of Toronto lends homeowners up to $125,000 for energy retrofits like heat pumps, solar and windows, repaid through the property tax bill at a fixed rate.
details: For owners of low-rise homes up to three storeys and six units
Fixed rates from 3.34% (5 years) to 4.75% (20 years), valid until September 30, 2026, plus a 2% admin charge
Apply online, then complete a home energy assessment before funding

sources.title: City of Toronto: Home Energy Loan Program

title: Basement flooding protection subsidy
summary: Toronto pays 80% of the cost of backwater valves, sump pumps and related work, up to $6,650 per property, for owners of houses up to fourplexes.
details: Backwater valve up to $1,600 each (two allowed), sump pump up to $2,250, plumbing assessment up to $500
Work must be done by a contractor with a valid Toronto business licence
Apply online within two years of the work; payment can take up to 10 weeks

sources.title: City of Toronto: Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program

title: Track your water use with MyWaterToronto
summary: A free city tool that shows your daily, weekly and monthly water use from your meter, which is the quickest way to spot a leak.
details: Sign up with the account and client number from your utility bill
Look for use that never drops to zero overnight; that usually means a leak
Works for houses and businesses with a City of Toronto utility account

sources.title: City of Toronto: MyWaterToronto

title: Prepare for a heavy-rain day
summary: Toronto's basement flooding page covers what to do before and during heavy rain: clear drains, move valuables up, and report flooding to 311.
details: Keep eavestroughs, downspouts and the storm drain by your curb clear of leaves
Disconnect downspouts from the sewer so roof water goes to the lawn
Report basement flooding or a surcharging sewer to 311

sources.title: City of Toronto: Basement Flooding

title: Bike Share Toronto
summary: City-owned bike share with regular bikes and e-bikes at stations across Toronto. Pay per ride, per day, or by the year.
details: Pay-as-you-go: $1 to unlock plus $0.12 a minute on a classic bike ($0.20 on an e-bike)
Day pass: $15 for unlimited 90-minute classic rides
Annual: $105 (30-minute rides) or $120 (45-minute rides), e-bikes half price per minute

sources.title: Bike Share Toronto: Pricing

title: Fair Pass transit discount
summary: Toronto residents aged 20 to 64 with low income get 36% off TTC fares: $2.10 a ride instead of $3.30, and no more than $98.70 a month.
details: Income must be below 75% of the Low-Income Measure; Ontario Works, ODSP and child care subsidy recipients qualify automatically
You need a PRESTO card number to apply
Apply online, by phone at 416-338-8888, or in person

sources.title: City of Toronto: Fair Pass Transit Discount Program

title: Plan a route on the cycling network map
summary: The city's interactive map shows every bike lane, trail and Bike Share station, with a route planner. A printed 2026 map is free at libraries and bike shops.
details: Enter your start address to plan a route on protected lanes where possible
Filter by bikeway type to avoid painted-lane-only streets
Pick up the paper map at any Toronto Public Library branch

sources.title: City of Toronto: Cycling Network Map

title: Charge an EV at a Green P lot
summary: Toronto's parking authority runs about 400 public chargers at Green P lots and on-street. Charging is billed separately from parking.
details: Level 2 off-street: $2 an hour, $6 overnight maximum
DC fast: $15 an hour (50 kW) or $20 an hour (100 kW)
Pay through the ChargePoint or Flo app; parking is paid separately in the Green P app

sources.title: Green P Parking: EV Charging

title: Curbside Green Bin pickup
summary: Toronto collects food scraps and other organics at the curb through the Green Bin program, on your regular garbage day.
details: Food scraps, coffee grounds, soiled paper and pet waste all go in
Not sure about an item? Search the city's Waste Wizard
Kitchen containers are $7 at Community Environment Days

sources.title: City of Toronto: What goes in my Green Bin

title: Community Environment Days
summary: From April to September, the city runs drop-off days in every ward: free compost to take home, and electronics and household hazardous waste to drop off.
details: Free bagged compost, two bags per household while supplies last
Drop off e-waste and up to 50 litres or 50 kg of household hazardous waste
Bring reusable clothing, books and sporting goods for donation

sources.title: City of Toronto: Community Environment Days

title: Repair Café Toronto
summary: A volunteer group that runs monthly events where fixers help you repair clothes, small appliances, bikes and electronics for free, instead of throwing them out.
details: Events are free; bring the broken item and stay to learn the fix
Check the events page for the next date and location
They're always looking for volunteer fixers

sources.title: Repair Café Toronto

title: Request a free street tree
summary: The city plants trees on the road allowance in front of homes and businesses at no cost. Property owners can request one through 311.
details: Submit a tree planting request online or by calling 311
The city picks a species suited to the site
Part of the plan to reach 40% canopy cover by 2050

sources.title: City of Toronto: Tree Planting on City Property

title: LEAF backyard tree planting
summary: A local nonprofit plants subsidized native trees on private property: an arborist consultation, delivery, planting and mulch for $160 to $230 a tree.
details: Native shrubs are $30 and cedars $50
Planting runs April to June and September to November
Apply online; earlier bookings get more species to choose from

sources.title: LEAF: Full Service Backyard Tree Planting

title: Join a community garden
summary: Around 60 community gardens across Toronto grow food, flowers and native plants together. Some donate harvests to local food programs.
details: Contact the Supervisor of Community Gardens Programs to join one near you
Some gardens have waiting lists
Want your own plot instead? See the city's allotment gardens

sources.title: City of Toronto: Community Gardens
